content.comment_body: Hello, I need to connect 1 condominium with 8 separate apartments, all sharing a single internet connection. Each apartment owner wants to control their own heating system. There are 8 [product_name] units (model [article_no]), each connected to a [product_name] module. The setup includes 1 available internet connection, 1 static IP, and 1 gateway. Is it possible for each apartment owner to have independent control—using a browser or [product_name] app? customer1 /[product_name] n.1 customer2 /[product_name] n.2 customer3 /[product_name] n.3... customer8 /[product_name] n.8? Thank you very much in advance!
Yes, this is possible—but each [product_name] must have its own IP address.

analysis.insight_summary: The user wants to create a remote-controlled heating system for 8 separate units within a condominium, each equipped with its own [product_name] module and requiring independent access despite sharing a single internet connection. Their primary concern is enabling secure and individual access—whether through a web browser or a mobile app—for each owner, without interference between the units. The response confirms the technical feasibility, noting that every [product_name] must have a distinct IP address, which introduces additional considerations for network setup and management.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expects each resident to be able to securely and independently operate their own device using either the [product_name] web interface or mobile app, even with only one shared internet connection.
